title: FP16 inference produces black images (NaN latents)
body:
First of all, thank you for the great model! 

Issue:
Running the model in the torch.float16 either in comfyui or diffusers results in pure black image. float32 works as intended but very slow on my PC. bfloat16 is upcast to float32 internally.

System specs:
OS: Windows 10
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 2060 (6 GB VRAM)
RAM: 16 GB
PyTorch: 2.9.1+cu130
Diffusers: 0.36
ComfyUI: latest version
NO triton or sage-attention.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run the basic comfyui workflow with startup flag --fp16-unet. 
Checked both quantized gguf model https://huggingface.co/jayn7/Z-Image-Turbo-GGUF/blob/main/z_image_turbo-Q4_K_M.gguf and https://huggingface.co/T5B/Z-Image-Turbo-FP8/blob/main/z-image-turbo-fp8-e4m3fn.safetensors.
Both of them produces black images (latent contains only nan values). 

2) Run diffusers workflow with https://huggingface.co/Disty0/Z-Image-Turbo-SDNQ-uint4-svd-r32 with provided code:
import torch
import diffusers
from sdnq import SDNQConfig # import sdnq to register it into diffusers and transformers

pipe = diffusers.ZImagePipeline.from_pretrained("Disty0/Z-Image-Turbo-SDNQ-uint4-svd-r32", torch_dtype=torch.float16)
pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload()

prompt = "any prompt"
image = pipe(
    prompt=prompt,
    height=1024,
    width=1024,
    num_inference_steps=9,
    guidance_scale=0.0,
    generator=torch.manual_seed(42),
).images[0]

→ Same result: black image. Inference in float32 works correctly, but is ~3× slower in ComfyUI and ~15× slower in Diffusers (no VRAM overflow—only partial CPU offloading occurs).

Notably:
Forcing torch.bfloat16 uses more VRAM than float32, yet inference speed remains the same as FP32 in Diffusers.
torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported() returns True, even though the RTX 20xx series does not support native BF16 compute (only storage); this may indicate emulation or a misleading runtime check.

In ComfyUI, --bf16-unet has no effect:
Model weight dtype: torch.bfloat16, manual cast: torch.float32

Observation:
The issue persists across differently quantized models (GGUF, FP8, SDNQ), suggesting the root cause is likely not quantization, but rather FP16 handling in the UNet or scheduler (e.g., overflow/underflow leading to NaNs in latents).

I hope something can be done here to fix the issue. Looking forward to your response.
